v7 What's new

Direct Uploads

Adds support for uploading single files directly (unzipped). Callers can set the new archive parameter to false to skip zipping the file during upload. Right now, we only support single files. The action will fail if the glob passed resolves to multiple files. The name parameter is also ignored with this setting. Instead, the name of the artifact will be the name of the uploaded file.

ESM

title: GH#31006: reclaim safe recovery caches within deadline
body:
## Summary

- Recognize ignored, untracked `__pycache__` and `.pytest_cache` directories at any depth, plus `.codegraph` only at the repository root, as regenerable recovery caches.
- Let mandatory exact remeasurement use the remaining automatic-maintenance deadline instead of the shorter default sizing timeout.
- Preserve fail-closed protection for tracked content, symlinks, nested `.codegraph`, arbitrary ignored data, failed Git queries, identity drift, and deadline exhaustion.

## Root cause

Recovery archive classification did not include the approved Python and CodeGraph cache identities. Separately, the second exact size measurement inherited the short global reporting timeout even when the automatic maintenance pass still had budget, so valid candidates could remain indefinitely unavailable.

## Safety decisions

- Repository-root-only cache identities use a dedicated allowlist rather than the any-depth component allowlist.
- Both status classification and archive pruning query tracked files before treating a recognized root as disposable.
- Git process-launch or query failures classify the archive as unavailable, never clear.
- The outer process-group deadline remains authoritative while the inner measurement receives only the calculated remaining budget.

## Verification

- `test-worktree-recovery-lifecycle.sh`: 36/36 passed.
- `test-cleanup-worktrees-async.sh`: 14/14 passed.
- `test-worktree-removal-audit.sh`: 50/50 passed.

## Summary

Resolves #31266.

- Fix a reproduced Linux authentication defect: the BSD-first UID probe emitted GNU filesystem output before falling back, contaminating the ownership comparison. Use the existing platform-dispatched stat helper instead; ownership and mode checks remain mandatory.
- Accept AskPass path aliases only when they reference the runtime's exact trusted executable, then normalize the sandbox value. Reject other executables, mismatched repository/identity, and invalid token artifacts with fixed, secret-free typed diagnostics.
- Run the exact producer environment through the runtime's authentication preflight synchronously before spawning. Repeated unchanged local rejections do not detach; launcher evidence remains available and existing attempt cleanup retains ownership of the rejected token.
- Preserve the credential across preflight and detached startup; synthetic tests prove cleanup occurs after readiness. No token values enter process arguments, diagnostics, or repository configuration.

## Files Changed

Only the six paths declared by the issue:

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-run.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/worker-token-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh`

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — synthetic credentials only, no model sessions or live smoke dispatch.
- Manual-dispatch suite: **83 passed, 0 failed**, including the real `headless-runtime-helper.sh run` preflight/import path and production producer, detach, validator, and cleanup functions across fresh processes. Only unrelated downstream worker setup is stubbed in the detached fixture.
- Headless-runtime suite: **273 passed, 0 failed**.
- ShellCheck 0.9.0: zero violations across all six scoped files. Pre-commit and pre-push checks pass.

Reproduce with `env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=<test-home> bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` and the same command for `test-headless-runtime-helper.sh`; both harnesses allocate disposable test homes. Isolating inherited runner settings avoids unrelated host-sensitive-temp failures and an intermittent existing GraphQL mock fallback failure. No host configuration or safety gate was changed.

The Linux UID defect is established by the existing AskPass fixture failing before the fix and passing afterward, plus GNU `stat -f` emitting filesystem text for the BSD probe. This does **not** claim to prove the cause of the original production incident. No live retry of another issue was performed.

## Review and Deferred Existing Findings

Independent read-only security/correctness review found no blocking introduced defects in the final bundle. Two confirmed pre-existing observations remain outside this repair:

1. Readiness can trust a stale deterministic detached log before child liveness (`dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`, `_dsi_wait_for_worker_readiness`; producer in `headless-runtime-worker-prepare.sh`, `_detach_worker`). Follow-up verification: seed an old readiness marker and launch a non-ready child; require attempt-bound readiness evidence. The detach producer is outside this brief's Files Scope.
2. title: GH#31309: Retire the legacy global peak-hours worker cap
body:
## Summary

Resolves #31309. Follow-up to #31241 and #31248; the maintainer explicitly corrected the peak-hours premise and authorized retirement in an interactive full-loop session.

- Remove the global peak-hours cap from `calculate_max_workers`.
- Keep `apply_peak_hours_cap` as a validated no-op for compatibility; old settings and environment overrides remain loadable but cannot throttle workers.
- Mark the legacy keys deprecated/ignored in settings help and documentation. Remove the obsolete enabling recommendation.
- Adapt existing characterization fixtures for enabled, disabled, overnight, alternate-host-timezone and invalid-timezone configurations.

title: GH#31356: fix stats dashboard and sweep starvation
body:
## Summary

- order health dashboards by their persisted refresh age before applying any explicit priority override
- stop optional dashboard iteration while the stats wrapper still has cleanup budget
- make daily quality sweeps resumable across scheduler runs with a topology-validated cursor and bounded per-repository execution

## Incident evidence

An installation with 21 pulse-enabled repositories repeatedly exhausted the 600-second stats-wrapper ceiling. title: GH#31356: fix: Bound and resume multi-repository stats work
body:
## Summary

Make scheduled stats work fair and resumable when all managed repositories cannot fit into one wrapper invocation.

- Order dashboards by canonical-operator refresh/attempt age, preserving the explicit priority override. Attempts never overwrite successful freshness state.
- Bound whole repository work, authentication/permission preflight, person-cache refresh and aggregate rendering against the existing wrapper deadline. Reserve time for quality work and cleanup; retain the outer watchdog.
- Persist a quality-sweep cursor atomically, reconcile current slug/path identities, advance after bounded failures, and write the daily timestamp only when the full eligible cycle has been admitted.
- Freeze each process before discovering/killing descendants to avoid spawning replacements during timeout cleanup. Remove attempt-owned temporary artifacts.

Resolves #31356

## Files and scope

- `.agents/scripts/stats-health-dashboard.sh`: fair ordering and bounded dashboard orchestration.
- `.agents/scripts/stats-quality-sweep.sh`: resumable, configuration-aware quality batches.
- `.agents/scripts/stats-shared.sh`: small shared deadline/child-containment primitives used by both existing orchestrators, avoiding duplicate implementations.
- Existing focused tests: `test-health-dashboard-identity-aliases.sh`, `test-stats-wrapper-timeout.sh`, `test-stats-wrapper-headless-export.sh`.

The wrapper, scheduler, maintainer authorization checks, privacy filters and remediation gates are unchanged. The headless test now recognizes the bounded cache call and the preserved-health-status behavior already introduced by #31089.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High — bounded child processes and persistent batch state.
- **Verification:** runtime-verified using isolated shell fixtures running the production orchestration/functions, with mocked external services. No production GitHub dashboard writes or reporter-host deployment were performed during development.
- All six focused suites passed: timeout/batch (8), headless/order (13), maintainer guard (1), serialization (28), identity/fairness (36), characterization (14): **100 assertions/test cases**, including a hanging repository, descendant cleanup, configuration add/remove, corrupt/completed cursor, expired admission, and slow permission preflight.
- ShellCheck on all six changed files: zero findings.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh`: exit 0, including Bash 3.2 compatibility, function-size, nesting, portability and secret checks. Historical formatting/string-literal advisories remain non-blocking; unrelated formatting was intentionally not swept into this fix.

## Decisions and independent review

The independent advisory review identified unbounded preflight and a descendant-spawn cleanup race; both were repaired and exercised by focused tests. The remaining suggested distinction between durable admission and the immediately following tool call was evaluated and rejected as an exactly-once requirement outside this best-effort scheduler contract: admission intentionally persists inside the admitted child before tool execution, so interruption cannot indefinitely pin later repositories. A visited entry means **attempt admitted**, never successful analysis. Errors/timeouts stay visible, no clean tool result is fabricated, and the next daily cycle retries every eligible repository. Moving that marker one function frame deeper would retain the same interruption window rather than provide transactional external-tool execution.

Defaults: whole health repository 60s, each optional health aggregate/cache phase 30s, quality repository 120s, existing health reserve 120s, quality cleanup reserve 5s in addition to the wrapper's existing 30s. All work is capped again by remaining absolute time. Repository-specific positive caps can be overridden with `STATS_HEALTH_REPO_TIMEOUT`, `STATS_HEALTH_AGGREGATE_TIMEOUT`, and `QUALITY_SWEEP_REPO_TIMEOUT`.

Rollback: revert these changes; the previous code ignores the new attempt/cursor files. Existing successful-refresh and daily timestamp formats are preserved.

## Release intent

The maintainer explicitly requested full-loop through patch release in the initiating interactive session. Release will use the canonical guarded release entry point after exact-head CI/review and observed merge, followed by publication/postflight/deployment verification. A live Linux/systemd canary on the reporter's installation is not claimed; development ran on macOS and publication checks remain separate.

title: fix: use available GitHub quota with adaptive admission
body:
## Summary

Use GitHub's available capacity for useful work instead of permanently withholding local quota reserves.

- Admit all available REST primary points with atomic in-flight accounting, including the final point; replace the four-request ceiling with the documented secondary-limit envelope for supported GETs.
- Pace only when observed demand predicts exhaustion before reset. Persist pacing deadlines across process restarts and rolling-history expiry; report local deferral reasons and retry times.
- Isolate unambiguous primary exhaustion by core, search, code-search and GraphQL resource. Preserve true secondary/Retry-After cooldowns and permission-error classification. Primary exhaustion no longer suppresses quota-status reads or unrelated pools.
- Make Pulse GraphQL scheduling hints reset-aware and remove the default REST hard reserve and guessed in-flight stage allowance. Keep explicit operator overrides and recovery after genuine throttling.
- Remove the default healthy-boot read ramp and document the policy in `.agents/reference/github-api-transport.md`.

## Implementation context

The request boundary is `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_budget.py` with `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_capacity.py`; primary cooldown classification lives in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-primary-cooldown.sh`, sourced by the existing shared cooldown owner. `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-budget-policy.sh` supplies the reset-aware window rule to Pulse. `.agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf` retains default-only configuration precedence.

## Runtime Testing

**runtime-verified**

- Exercised the changed `gh` shim against the live repository metadata endpoint: successful response and response-owned local admission status (`remaining=1274`, `reserved=0`, `floor=0`). No artificial quota exhaustion was induced against GitHub.
- Existing hermetic shim harness: **161 passed, 0 failed**, including core exhaustion followed by a successful search request and quota-status recovery through the normal CLI boundary.
- REST admission suite: **33 tests passed**, including final-point accounting, concurrency, long pacing deadlines, process reopen, uncertain spend, reset recovery, Retry-After and paced-read queueing within the normal timeout.
- Circuit-breaker suite: **51/51 passed**; Pulse priority suite and **33** configuration-precedence assertions passed; timeout regression passed.
- Shared cooldown suite passed, including unrelated-pool isolation, generic forbidden responses, abuse and recovery ramps.
- `bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed` passed: ShellCheck, secret checks, Markdown and applicable complexity/portability ratchets. Existing unrelated formatting/size advisories remain unchanged.

## Review and decisions

Independent review identified loss of pacing evidence after 60 seconds; fixed by persisting reset-keyed pacing separately and added regression coverage. Live merge validation then exposed the old two-second admission wait rejecting normally paced reads; the follow-up queues these within the normal read timeout, with passing back-to-back live metadata and branch-protection reads. Focused independent review found no material defects. Final branch evidence bundle: `b2e8629ec98e70e4701c27c740251b874b5860afcd472f9ed916e549b70ab0bf`.

This is local coordination for supported authenticated REST GETs, not complete wire-level or fleet-wide quota accounting. Opaque native CLI commands and mutations retain native execution with shared cooldown protection. These checks prove behaviour, not a production throughput percentage. Evaluate completed work and latency without repeated throttling, rather than call-count reductions alone.

## Summary

Resolves #31378.

Complete the bundled issue-acceptance and exact protected-source ceremony, rather than another prerequisite-only change. One explicit human decision independently signs the issue verdict and a narrow V3 source capability. Issue-only approval never becomes source authority.

## Delivered

- Durable, bounded, revocable proposals retain exact metadata, not source contents. Stable references survive delayed attendance; grant TTL starts at confirmation. Changed source is explicitly redisplayed for consent; a different runtime/session/worktree cannot silently replace the original context.
- Trusted fixed-origin GitHub verification reconstructs the issue snapshot. Credentials and issue mutations execute only after dropping privileges; the root broker never executes user-managed helpers as root. Issue and source signatures use separate keys and namespaces.
- Journaled publication handles uncertain GitHub responses, duplicate invocation, cancellation and crash recovery without reposting, resigning or expanding authority. Receipt and all immutable snapshots publish atomically behind private per-user storage.
- Native runtime context binds UID/PID, runtime instance, fresh SDK session generation, project, repository and owned linked worktree. Environment values only locate the socket; they do not confer authority.
- CLI and composed OpenCode Read consume the same exact manifest. Verified Write/Edit/apply_patch cycles preserve bounded same-session continuity; changed members require current observed-edit proof while unchanged members remain independently usable.
- Legacy commands and V1/V2 semantics remain separate. Unsupported or mismatched broker/plugin combinations fail closed. Setup retains its signed-release dependency closure and never silently elevates for maintenance.

## Acceptance evidence

| Required behavior | Evidence |

| One decision for issue plus protected source and existing test | Real bundle issuer fixture with generated independent signing keys and fake GitHub publication; conventional regression-test discovery and batch routing fixtures |
| Stable approval after 24 hours/seven days; confirmation-time TTL | Controlled-clock Python proposal and approval tests; no assistant-side reissue required |
| Multi-path CLI and Read agreement | Atomic V3 fixture invokes real Python issuer and native runtime IPC, then verifies and reads both exact paths through CLI/composed Read |
| Direct-edit/read continuity without another prompt | Write, Edit and apply_patch integration cycles, including CLI verification of memory-only observed metadata |
| Identity, links, credentials, extra paths and replay denied | Python and Node negative cases; no legacy issue-only authority backfill |
| Cancellation, expiry, duplicate invocation and partial failure | Journal/tombstone tests, lost-response retry, crash-after-rename recovery, source drift and context mismatch tests |
| Legacy and mixed-version behavior | Existing receipt suites and signed-release broker setup suite |
| Independent final security review | CodeRabbit closeout at exact head linked below, reusing unchanged issuer review |

## Files and reference patterns

- `.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh`, `source-access-helper.sh`, `interactive-start-helper.sh`: combined command routing, explicit human-terminal elevation and powerless preflight.

title: GH#31548: preserve Beads hook chaining and bound privacy diff scans
body:
## Summary

Resolves #31548

Preserve a complete trailing Beads integration section when refreshing the
canonical post-checkout dispatcher, and make that section reachable after a
successful guard check.

The previous dispatcher used `exec` or exited before appended Beads code, while
the installer replaced the whole managed hook during refresh. This change fixes
both control flow and refresh preservation without weakening guard failures.

The pre-push path also exposed expensive per-line privacy scanning and PEM state
leaking between unrelated files. A follow-up commit conservatively filters
built-in candidates in one streaming pass, keeps original file/line reporting,
and scopes PEM state to each file. Custom inventories retain the full scan.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/install-canonical-guard.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/test-canonical-guard.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/privacy-guard-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/test-privacy-guard.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-privacy-diff-fast-path.sh`

## Safety behaviour

- Propagate nonzero guard results before running Beads.
- Preserve one complete trailing Beads section, including matching versioned
  markers; refuse malformed, duplicate, mismatched, or ambiguous sections.
- Stage and syntax-check output before replacing the installed hook.
- Refuse symlink/non-regular targets and uninstalling a mixed Beads hook.
- Retain existing Beads section policies rather than silently changing them.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/test-canonical-guard.sh`: 24 tests passed.
- The same suite passed with a reviewed real-world hook supplied as a local
  fixture, including an actual Git file checkout in a synthetic repository.
- ShellCheck passed on all changed shell files; formatting passed on the hook
  repair files, with existing advisory formatting debt in the privacy helpers.
- Privacy regression suites passed: 21 fast-path/file-state cases, 27 guard
  cases, and 18 public-write cases. The cache-refresh case now uses the supported
  probe stub instead of making a live GitHub request from an offline test suite.
- A large inherited upstream comparison completed in 10.29 seconds and still
  blocked key-header literals, rather than timing out after 300 seconds. The
  actual repair diff passed the privacy hook against its upstream base in 4.40
  seconds. These are local observations, not universal performance guarantees.
- Changed-file local quality checks, explicit secret scans, and pre-commit
  validation passed without disabling checks.
- An earlier expanded suite reproduced nine failures against the old installer.

Tests use an isolated HOME and a controlled Beads stub; they do not mutate a
real task database. A post-checkout hook detects state after checkout, not before.

## Review and rollout

Review-only request. Do not auto-merge or deploy. A project hook repair alone is
not update-durable while its installer still discards the Beads section. Review
framework delivery and downstream activation together. No private project data,
local paths, credentials, or production content are included in this request.

  • Ignore "validate" option when command is "complete" (otherwise errors with invalid option)

v2.0.0 (2025-08-05)

This release mirrors the breaking change we introduced in the qlty CLI proper: we now validate coverage data by default instead of uploading coverage data to qlty that qlty cannot use. Now you must opt out of this behavior whereas previously opt in.

What This Means for You:

  • If coverage reporting is working as expected, you'll experience no impact. If you're uploading valid reports and seeing directory and file-level coverage metrics in Qlty, you don't need to do anything. (If your reports include mismatched paths, you'll see specific path errors listed within your CI output)
  • Potential CI Build Failures: Once this change is implemented, if your current CI/CD pipeline uploads a report with mismatched paths, your builds will begin to fail when executing qlty coverage publish.
  • Quick Fix for Build Failures: If your builds start failing and you need to get them passing immediately, you can temporarily add validate: false to the GitHub Action configuration. This will disable validation and allow your CI build to pass (though your coverage data will remain broken until you've uploaded a valid report).

title: GH#31617: make Pulse productivity evidence bounded and actionable
body:
## Summary

- Bound productivity collection and return component timings, timeout states and partial queue coverage instead of silent hangs.
- Inventory repositories with four bounded independent reads before dependency/progress enrichment; preserve existing GitHub admission and ownership gates.
- Keep absent capacity unknown, reject stale/future cycle and health snapshots as current occupancy, and identify configured maximums separately.
- Add optional `--verify-delivery` without dividing independently observed GitHub deliveries by local terminal attempts.
- Document how to turn supply, admission, integration and missing-evidence measurements into the next bounded action.

Resolves #31617

## Files and reference patterns

Existing collector, queue, dependency, current-state and jq report paths are modified: `.agents/scripts/pulse-check-helper.sh`, `pulse-check-queue-scan.py`, `pulse_check_dependencies.py`, `pulse-current-state.py`, and `pulse-check-report.jq`. Existing tests `test-pulse-check-helper.sh` and `test-pulse-current-state-helper.sh` cover the changes. `.agents/reference/diagnostics-discipline.md` explains scope and interpretation. No new runner, database, daemon or always-loaded rules.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk:** medium; runtime-verified read-only production diagnostics plus existing isolated failure fixtures.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-check-helper.sh`:162 assertions passed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-current-state-helper.sh`:passed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-current-state-guardrails.sh`:23 tests passed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`:all required local checks passed; existing formatting advisory remains.
- Real `pulse-check-helper.sh json --budget 60 --window 15m --since 6h --verify-delivery` returned usable evidence in approximately43 seconds:21/21 repository inventories, explicitly incomplete enrichment, a10-second API collector timeout, and two verified deliveries independently of one terminal local attempt. This is one observation, not a benchmark or a sustained throughput claim.

## Review and safety

Independent review found nested-deadline loss of partial output and stale health-snapshot fallback; both were corrected and covered by focused regressions. Re-review found no remaining blocking defect. Current-state, missing-capacity, incomplete-scan and trust/permission tests remain fail-closed.

The live queue also exposed duplicate Dependabot intake targeting the same PR. Ownership changed before mutation, so no live worker was closed or displaced. Independent follow-up #31618 tracks that defect; this PR does not claim it solved or count issue entries as independent work targets.

Fresh dispatch/merge authorization, atomic admission, local-first idle ordering, the existing 300-second cooldown/recovery defaults, and typed unknown outcomes are unchanged. title: GH#31678: persist worker permission handoffs
body:
## Summary

- Retry permission-request comments and blocker-label writes, verifying ambiguous writes before retrying.
- Keep captured permission events active until the GitHub handoff is durable.
- Reject non-grantable requests before applying `needs-maintainer-permissions`.
- Prevent Pulse forced re-evaluation from falsely declaring an active `needs-simplification` gate cleared.

## Root cause

The worker retired captured request evidence before confirming the issue handoff, while GitHub writes had no bounded retry/read-after-write path. Separately, simplification triage interpreted the generic active-worker skip result as proof that the label had been cleared, producing a false CLEARED comment while the label remained and later hid the issue from dispatch.

## Runtime Testing

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-permission-grant-verification.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-reeval-stale-continuation.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-completion-tests.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`
- Independent closeout review of bundle `b0788ec2f71a882e81a05d64d9db65ec3aefce9423e044f466f31d85eaafa607`: CLEAN

## Decisions

title: GH#31678: persist worker permission handoffs
body:
## Summary

- Retry permission-request comments and blocker-label writes, verifying ambiguous writes before retrying.
- Keep captured permission events active until the GitHub handoff is durable.
- Reject non-grantable requests before applying `needs-maintainer-permissions`.
- Prevent Pulse forced re-evaluation from falsely declaring an active `needs-simplification` gate cleared.

## Root cause

The worker retired captured request evidence before confirming the issue handoff, while GitHub writes had no bounded retry/read-after-write path. Separately, simplification triage interpreted the generic active-worker skip result as proof that the label had been cleared, producing a false CLEARED comment while the label remained and later hid the issue from dispatch.

The original orphan-recovery PR #31689 retained a stale merge base and attributed unrelated `main` complexity to this change. This replacement preserves its implementation on a clean current-main branch without force-pushing worker history.

## Runtime Testing

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-permission-grant-verification.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-reeval-stale-continuation.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-completion-tests.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`
- Independent closeout review: CLEAN (`101608bde154f22073427f79ab54ed3bd410366f932e306df8e47b8eef7e88ca`)

## Decisions

- Bounded retries default to three attempts with read-after-write verification for idempotency.
- Grantability is checked defensively at the persistence boundary even when the broker should already reject the request.
- Active simplification work retains the real gate result; only confirmed label removal may emit CLEARED.

Resolves #31678

title: GH#31842: perf: narrow Supervisor Pulse project scope
body:
## Summary

- narrow the Supervisor Pulse OpenCode project root from the complete retained agent workspace to its dedicated `supervisor` subtree
- apply the same default to direct runtime configuration, generated Linux systemd environments, and generated macOS launchd plists
- preserve explicit `PULSE_DIR` overrides and all existing supervision behavior

## Evidence and scope

OpenCode 1.18.30 supplies its `--dir` project as FFF's `basePath`. Upstream report anomalyco/opencode#46256 independently reports sustained reads that scale with a multi-million-file project, but equivalence with the production observations in #31842 is not claimed.

An aggregate, warm-cache local inventory measured the effective default scopes without reading file contents:

| Scope | Directories | Files | Logical bytes | Enumeration |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Previous agent-workspace root | 165,609 | 1,845,867 | 197,863,483,766 | 51.575 s |
| Dedicated supervisor subtree | 2,711 | 46,894 | 1,820,116,949 | 0.256 s |

This reduces the default candidate scope by 98.4% of directories, 97.5% of files, and 99.1% of logical bytes while keeping the same Pulse prompt, model, cadence, tools, and state files. Both inventory passes reported zero filesystem input blocks because the data was cached; these figures demonstrate scope reduction, not post-deployment I/O causality.

title: fix(pulse): converge generated worker intake
body:
## Summary

- elect one canonical Dependabot worker intake even when GitHub returns matching issues newest-first
- reconcile idle cross-runner duplicate intakes without closing active work
- generate canonical `### Files Scope` sections for large-file debt issues
- distinguish malformed generated briefs from duplicate-lookup uncertainty during pre-dispatch validation

## Root cause

Dependabot intake creation reused the first matching API result while dispatch independently preferred active work or the oldest idle issue. Separate Pulse hosts could therefore disagree about ownership and preserve duplicate generated tasks. Large-file debt briefs also placed their edit target outside the canonical worker scope section, causing pre-dispatch validation to reject them with the same status previously used for uncertain duplicate lookups.

title: fix(pulse): bound diagnostics and retire terminal retry hints
body:
## Summary

- Replace repeated per-line Bash API-log counting with streaming awk field comparisons, keeping pulse-check's existing collector deadline.
- Retire closed/merged PR retry hints only after claiming their queue generation and re-fetching authoritative state. Preserve reopened PRs, failed reads, and newer events.
- Fix the stats quarantine permission regression test on GNU/Linux using the existing Python dependency instead of incompatible stat format fallback.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `bash .agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-helper.sh api-budget --json`

**Actual output:** On a long-lived API log, elapsed time was 39.36 seconds, exceeding pulse-check's 10-second API collector deadline. The report marked API collection timed_out. Merge logs also repeatedly retained already-merged exact retry targets, consuming the bounded priority target list.

**Expected output:** Diagnostics fit the existing collection deadline; authoritatively terminal retry generations leave the queue without losing concurrent new events.

## Implementation and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-helper.sh`: use TSV fields 2 and 6, consistent with the existing awk cache summaries.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`: reuse `_pulse_merge_queue_begin`, `_pulse_merge_queue_refresh_object`, and `_pulse_merge_queue_finish`; no direct SQLite deletion or gate bypass.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-pr-backlog-priority.sh`: isolated real queue coverage for MERGED, CLOSED, reopened, API-error, concurrent-event and unknown-state cases.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stats-helper.sh`: portable quarantine mode assertion.

title: fix(worker): execute blocker CLIs through deployment symlinks
body:
## Summary

Fix silent no-op execution of both worker blocker CLI entrypoints through symlink-based runtime deployments. Compare canonical filesystem paths for argv[1] and the module URL instead of comparing an unresolved argv URL with Node's resolved module URL. Imports remain side-effect free; invalid/unavailable entry paths fail closed.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `node <symlinked-scripts>/worker-blocker-cli.mjs unknown-command`

**Actual output:** No output and exit 0, because the direct-execution guard does not match and command dispatch is never called. The deployed stale-supervisor resolution command likewise returned exit 0 without applying reconciliation. Invoking with `--preserve-symlinks-main` proved the command itself worked.

**Expected output:** Unknown commands return exit 2. Valid commands execute exactly once, including when the scripts directory contains a deployment symlink.

## Files and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/worker-blocker-log.mjs`: shared canonical-path entrypoint predicate, preserving the existing guarded CLI dispatch.
- `.agents/scripts/worker-blocker-cli.mjs`: reuse that predicate.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-worker-blocker-log.mjs`: existing subprocess test pattern, with an isolated symlinked scripts directory, actual append verification and unknown-command exit checks for both entrypoints.

## Verification

- `node --check .agents/scripts/worker-blocker-cli.mjs`
- `node --check .agents/scripts/worker-blocker-log.mjs`
- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-worker-blocker-log.mjs`: 14 passed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`: passed.

## Runtime Testing

runtime-verified: existing Node subprocess tests invoke both actual entrypoints through a symlinked scripts directory without special Node flags. Each writes one valid event to its isolated log; unknown commands return 2. Existing reconciliation, identity preservation, symlink-log refusal and concurrent append tests remain passing. No production permission grants or task-gate changes.

## Scope

This fixes CLI execution and evidence recording, not task authorisation. It does not clear issue-specific permission blockers, revise worker briefs, redispatch held tasks or publish a version release.
